# Electrode-count study (supplementary, post-test; generated by scripts/analyze_electrode_study.py)

New runs: 703 (388 in the first wave, 315 in the second). Seeds 0-2 of the archived conditions come from results/test; everything else is new. Accuracy is on artifact-free session-2 trials, FP32 unless stated, seeds averaged within participant. Intervals resample the nine participants; the seed standard error holds the participants fixed and reflects training randomness only.

## Is it seed luck?

Drawing 3 of the 10 seeds at random for each participant and model, the nine-participant mean difference comes out as:

- relevance-16 minus full-22: mean +1.30 pp, SD 0.88 pp, central 95% [-0.44, +3.01], at or below zero in 7% of draws
- relevance-8 minus full-22: mean -4.20 pp, SD 0.81 pp, central 95% [-5.80, -2.64], at or below zero in 100% of draws

Averaging the class probabilities of the ten seeds of each model into one prediction removes most run-to-run variance. A difference caused by that variance would shrink:

- mean single run: 64.25% with 22 electrodes, 65.57% with 16 (+1.31 pp)
- ten-seed average: 67.88% with 22 electrodes, 69.79% with 16 (+1.91 pp)
- two seeds of the same model give the same label on 71.6% of trials with 22 electrodes and 73.7% with 16

## Who gains: participants grouped by their accuracy with all 22 electrodes

Below 60% with 22 electrodes: P2, P4, P5, P6. Above: P1, P3, P7, P8, P9. The split was chosen after seeing the results, and the groups have four and five people, so this describes these participants and is not a tested hypothesis. Rank correlation between a participant's 22-electrode accuracy and the gain from 16 electrodes: -0.67 (n = 9, p = 0.05).
